overview.description: Mixing your own media is cheap and self-sufficient: protein, yeast extract, salt, water and agar. Antibiotic media is 'biotech on easy mode' - a few drops purge anything without your plasmid. The only catch is a little maths for antibiotic dilutions.
objectives: mix LB liquid media and LB-agar from scratch
prepare antibiotic stock solutions and selection plates

steps.intro: Mixing your own media is cheap and self-sufficient: protein, yeast extract, salt, water and agar. Antibiotic media is 'biotech on easy mode' - a few drops purge anything without your plasmid. The only catch is a little maths for antibiotic dilutions.

instructions.title: Mix LB liquid media
instructions.description: Combine tryptone, yeast extract and NaCl in water, then sterilise. This is your standard E. coli media.

instructions.title: Make LB-agar
instructions.description: Add agar to LB before sterilising. Cool to ~50C before pouring so it doesn't kill antibiotics.

instructions.title: Add antibiotics
instructions.description: Once the agar is hand-warm, add antibiotic from a frozen stock at the working concentration, swirl, and pour.

instructions.title: Pour plates
instructions.description: Pour a thin even layer, flame off bubbles, let set, then dry lid-ajar before storing inverted at 4C.

submission.description: Pour a set of LB-agar plates (plain and antibiotic). Photograph them and report your antibiotic working concentration and stock dilution maths.
